data: How about this for this month: I take 6 tons, and John, Kate, Jack, and Emma each take 11? I’ll choose 6 tons this month. That would give me $6,000 and each of you $11,000. If everyone accepts and follows that allocation, our total catch is 50 tons, leaving 50 to reproduce back to 100. We can discuss a different split next month; this isn’t a binding future arrangement. John, would you be willing to choose 11, and would the others agree to the same?

I’ll agree to 11 tons this month, Luke, though you shouldn’t have to take less every month. Keeping the total at 50 means we can earn a living without depleting the lake our village depends on. John, Jack, Emma—will you each commit to 11 as well?

I’ll take 11 tons this month. Thanks, Luke, for offering to take less, but let’s aim for an equal 10 tons each next month so everyone shares the income fairly and the lake stays healthy. John, can you commit to 11 this month?

I’ll commit to 11 tons this month. My family taught me to leave enough fish for the next catch, and this plan does that. Thanks, Luke—I support discussing an equal 10-ton share next month. John, are you on board with 11?

I’m on board—I’ll take 11 tons this month. That settles our total at 50, leaving enough for the lake to replenish. Thanks, Luke. Next month, I support 10 tons each so we all share equally and keep our village’s livelihood secure.
Thanks, everyone—we’ve all agreed for this month. I’ll honor my 6-ton catch, with each of you choosing 11. Next month, let’s revisit the split, starting with the equal 10-ton proposal.
